prompts.text: Name a city in France.
prompts.hint: Think beyond the capital, toward ports and regional centres.
prompts.fact: The Seine reaches the sea near Le Havre, downstream of Paris and Rouen.

prompts.text: Name a city in Japan.
prompts.hint: Think of the islands of Honshu, Hokkaido, Kyushu and Shikoku.
prompts.fact: Kyoto served as Japan’s imperial capital for more than a thousand years.

prompts.text: Pick a city in Brazil.
prompts.hint: Coastal cities and inland state capitals both count.
prompts.fact: Brasília replaced Rio de Janeiro as Brazil’s capital in 1960.

prompts.text: Name a chemical element whose symbol has just one letter.

answers.name: Yttrium
answers.note: Named after Ytterby, a village in Sweden.

prompts.hint: You may enter the element name or its one-letter symbol.
prompts.fact: Tungsten’s symbol W comes from the name wolfram.

prompts.text: Name an SI base unit or an SI derived unit with a special name.

answers.name: Katal
answers.note: The SI unit of catalytic activity.

prompts.hint: Think of the seven base units plus named derived units.
prompts.fact: The SI has seven base units; the newton is a derived unit of force.

prompts.text: Name a scientist who received a Nobel Prize in Physics before 2000.
prompts.hint: Think of quantum theory, particles and radiation.
prompts.fact: Marie Curie shared the 1903 physics prize before winning chemistry in 1911.

prompts.text: Name a feature film directed by Hayao Miyazaki, released by the end of 2023.

answers.name: Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind
The Castle of Cagliostro
aliases: Lupin III The Castle of Cagliostro
answers.note: Miyazaki’s first feature as director, released in 1979.

prompts.hint: Think of Studio Ghibli and Miyazaki’s earlier adventure film.

prompts.text: Name a feature film directed by Steven Spielberg with a US theatrical release from 1974 through 2019.

answers.name: Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom
Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade
Close Encounters of the Third Kind
Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull

prompts.hint: Adventure, history and science fiction all offer choices.
prompts.fact: Spielberg’s first US theatrical feature in this date range is The Sugarland Express.

prompts.text: Name a Tom Hanks movie released before 2020.

answers.name: A Beautiful Day in the Neighborhood

prompts.hint: Animated voice performances count alongside on-screen roles.
prompts.fact: Tom Hanks voices Woody in the first four Toy Story features.

prompts.text: Name a musical instrument normally played with a bow.

answers.name: Igil
answers.note: A bowed string instrument associated with Tuva.

prompts.hint: Think beyond the western string section.
prompts.fact: An erhu traditionally has two strings and is played with a bow between them.

prompts.text: Name a studio album by the Beatles (UK core catalogue, plus Magical Mystery Tour).

answers.name: Sgt. Pepper’s Lonely Hearts Club Band

prompts.hint: Think of the core UK albums; Magical Mystery Tour also counts.
prompts.fact: The Beatles’ self-titled 1968 album is commonly called the White Album.

prompts.text: Name a composer born before 1900 who wrote orchestral music.
prompts.hint: Think of orchestral composers across several centuries.
prompts.fact: Dvořák wrote his Ninth Symphony while working in the United States.

prompts.text: Name a sport where a ball goes over a net.
prompts.hint: The ball must cross a net to reach the opposition.
prompts.fact: Sepak takraw uses a woven ball and players primarily strike it with their feet.

prompts.text: Name a country that won the men’s FIFA World Cup from 1930 through 2022, or hosted it in that period.
prompts.hint: Either winning or hosting qualifies, through the 2022 edition.

prompts.text: Name a type of athletics event on the Tokyo 2020 programme (held in 2021; no gender needed).
prompts.hint: You do not need to specify men’s, women’s or mixed.

prompts.text: Name a person who served as president of the United States before 1900.
prompts.hint: The cutoff is the end of 1899.
prompts.fact: Grover Cleveland served two non-consecutive terms in the nineteenth century.

prompts.text: Name an ancient Egyptian pharaoh.

answers.name: Hatshepsut
answers.note: A woman who ruled ancient Egypt as pharaoh.

prompts.hint: Women who held the title pharaoh qualify too.
prompts.fact: Hatshepsut ruled Egypt as pharaoh during the eighteenth dynasty.

prompts.text: Name a city that had a Roman amphitheatre whose remains survive.
prompts.hint: Look beyond Rome to surviving arenas around the former empire.

prompts.text: Name a hot soup or stew.
prompts.hint: Choose a hot preparation rather than a chilled soup.
prompts.fact: Miso soup takes its name from fermented soybean paste.

prompts.text: Name a type of bread or flatbread.
prompts.hint: Leavened loaves and unleavened flatbreads both count.
prompts.fact: Sourdough fermentation uses a living culture of yeasts and bacteria.

prompts.text: Name a plant grown for an edible part underground.
prompts.hint: The edible part may grow beneath the soil.
prompts.fact: Ginger is a rhizome, while an onion is a bulb.

prompts.text: Name a fruit people eat fresh.
prompts.hint: Use the everyday culinary meaning, not a botanical classification.
prompts.fact: A strawberry’s tiny surface structures each contain a seed.

prompts.text: Name a spice, rather than a leaf herb.
prompts.hint: Think of seeds, bark, roots and dried fruits used as seasonings.
prompts.fact: Cinnamon is made from the inner bark of certain trees.

prompts.text: Name a dish made mainly with rice.
prompts.hint: The rice should be central to the dish.
prompts.fact: Risotto is made by gradually cooking rice with added liquid.

prompts.text: Name an edible bean, pea, lentil or other legume.
prompts.hint: Peas, lentils and familiar beans all count.
prompts.fact: Peanuts belong to the legume family rather than the tree-nut group.

prompts.text: Name a dessert.
prompts.hint: Baked, chilled and fried sweets all count.
prompts.fact: Panna cotta means cooked cream in Italian.

prompts.text: Name a sauce or condiment for savoury food.
prompts.hint: Think of a finishing sauce, dip, spread or table condiment.
prompts.fact: Traditional pesto gets its green colour from basil leaves.

prompts.text: Name a marsupial (a species or familiar group).
prompts.hint: Think of Australian species and American opossums.
prompts.fact: Marsupials typically give birth to relatively undeveloped young.

prompts.text: Name a kind of shark.
prompts.hint: Large filter-feeders count alongside predatory sharks.
prompts.fact: The whale shark is a filter-feeding fish, not a whale.

prompts.text: Name a plant grown for its flowers.
prompts.hint: Think of flowering ornamentals rather than foliage plants.
prompts.fact: A sunflower head consists of many small individual flowers.

prompts.text: Name a kind of snake.
prompts.hint: Do not include legless lizards.
prompts.fact: Snakes are reptiles, and their scales are made largely of keratin.

prompts.text: Name a butterfly species with a common English name.
prompts.hint: Choose a butterfly rather than a moth.
prompts.fact: Butterflies pass through egg, larva, pupa and adult stages.

prompts.text: Name a kind of wild cat.
prompts.hint: Small wild cats count as well as lions and tigers.
prompts.fact: A cheetah is a cat, but it is not in the genus Panthera.

prompts.text: Name a sea mammal.
prompts.hint: Think of whales, dolphins, seals and their relatives.
prompts.fact: Dolphins breathe air through a blowhole rather than extracting oxygen from water.

prompts.text: Name a bird of prey, including owls and vultures.
prompts.hint: Owls and vultures are included in this clue.
prompts.fact: An owl’s facial disc helps direct sound toward its ears.

prompts.text: Name a conifer tree (a genus, species or familiar group).
prompts.hint: Think of cone-bearing tree groups.
prompts.fact: Larches are conifers that shed their needles each year.

prompts.text: Name a first-stage starter Pokémon offered in the first four generations of the main games (Grass, Fire or Water starters only).
prompts.hint: Only the initial Grass, Fire and Water choices from generations one to four count.

prompts.hint: Think of planets, asteroids, comets and the Sun.

prompts.hint: Planetary probes and astronomy observatories both count.

prompts.hint: Consider wavelengths beyond visible light.

prompts.hint: Use the agency name or familiar abbreviation.

prompts.text: Name an astronomer born before 1900.
prompts.hint: Ancient observers and telescope pioneers both count.

prompts.text: Name a woman known for research in astronomy or astrophysics.

prompts.text: Name a named surface feature on Mars.
prompts.hint: Mountains, craters, plains and valleys all count.

prompts.text: Name a named impact crater on Earth’s Moon.

prompts.text: Name an annually recurring meteor shower.

prompts.text: Name a unit used to describe astronomical distances, sizes, times, masses or brightness.

prompts.text: Give an abbreviation used for a space agency, telescope, mission, orbit or spaceflight system.
